data.description:
# fsck should RECOVER, not just refuse

Change 1557 (bug b636) makes the snapshot rebuild FAIL CLOSED when the prior SNAPSHOT cites
source events absent from disk. That stops new corruption, but it leaves the existing
population permanently un-repairable: a dry run of the fixed fsck reports 505 live tickets
in exactly that shape, and `fsck --repair` can now never drive them to fsck-zero.

## Evidence that recovery is possible
The deleted event files are still in `origin/tickets` history (compaction deleted them from
the worktree; the blobs remain reachable at the deleting commit's parent). Measured over the
505 flagged tickets: 504 have deletion records covering every cited-missing uuid, 1 partial,
0 with no record at all.

Validated end-to-end on a COPY of the live store: restoring every event compaction ever
deleted for a ticket (from the deletion index, not just the newest snapshot's citation list)
and then rebuilding restored 214/214 of the already-regressed tickets to their correct
status, 486 events recovered.

## Why the citation list is not enough
Ticket 72d5 recovered its close STATUS but still read in_progress: an EARLIER deleted STATUS
that no surviving snapshot cites broke the chain's current_status precondition, so the
reducer rejected both it and the close. Recovery must sweep the ticket's full deletion
history, not the newest snapshot's source_event_uuids.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `recover_deleted_sources(tracker, ticket_id, ticket_dir)` restores every event file
      deleted from the ticket dir in tickets-branch history, writing each back as a folded
      `.retired` source (never resurrecting it as a live event).
- [ ] The fsck repair path attempts recovery BEFORE deciding to refuse: recover -> re-check
      `snapshot_missing_sources` -> rebuild if now complete; only refuse (b636 fail-closed)
      when recovery cannot complete the log.
- [ ] `--dry-run` reports what WOULD be recovered and rebuilt, writing nothing.
- [ ] Recovery is scoped per ticket (`git log --diff-filter=D -- <tid>/`), not a full-history
      index build, so it stays usable on a large store.
- [ ] Held-out test: a ticket whose close exists ONLY in history is recovered and reads
      closed again after `fsck --repair`.
- [ ] A ticket with genuinely unrecoverable sources still refuses and is surfaced.
data.title: fsck: auto-recover deleted SNAPSHOT sources from tickets history, then rebuild
